the best way to identify social ties from email communication data in a population of employees is to use logistic regression to predict ties, then use the thresholding method that best matches the network metrics of interest, and then use the threshold that best predicts the autocorrelation of health traits.

we found that logistic regression predicted a greater proportion of offline social relationships than did the other two methods, that the threshold method produced the best match between the offline network and the online network in terms of network metrics, and that ranked email partners demonstrated a greater degree of correlation of BMI across social ties than did the other methods.
we found a method that infers social relationships based on email traffic data that can be used for social network analysis.

the use of email communication data to infer social networks among coworkers.

the development and validation of methods for inferring health-related social networks from online communication data.

all of these methods have strengths and limitations and that researchers should consider their own research goals and available data when choosing a method.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best approach to inferring health-related social networks among coworkers is to combine the three techniques described in this study.
email communication data can be used to infer social networks that have similar properties to offline social networks, and that the best method depends on the research question.
email traffic can be a valuable data source for inferring social networks and that the methods we tested are promising for this purpose, with some limitations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
email communication can be a valuable source of data for studying social networks and health.
email communication data can be used to identify health-related social ties among coworkers, and that different methods may be appropriate depending on the research question of interest.

email traffic can be used to generate a network map that is comparable to a survey-based social network map in an employee population, and that email-based network maps can be used to study social influences on health-related behavior in the workplace.
